name: CSS for JavaScript Developers
tagline: Interactive self-paced CSS course for React and Vue developers
team: Solo, plus a part-time contractor a few hours a week for support and captioning (2021)
timeToFirstDollar: About 7 months: started the course in August 2020 and opened the pre-sale in March 2021 (after a few quiet direct sales to people who had emailed him)
summary: Josh W. Comeau, a front-end developer known for his interactive blog, left his job at Gatsby in 2020 and built a CSS course on his own platform. A one-week early-access pre-sale in March 2021 brought in about $550K against a $50K goal. He later released a second course, The Joy of React (2023).
origin: Comeau worked at Khan Academy, DigitalOcean, Concordia University and Gatsby Inc. (as a Staff Software Engineer). After a repetitive stress injury he left his job in summer 2020 and started the course in August. Over 2020 he grew from about 10k Twitter followers and 1k email subscribers to 31k followers and about 28k subscribers, helped by viral blog posts and a free book. With the course roughly half done, he opened a one-week pre-sale on March 10-16, 2021.
howItMakesMoney: One-time purchase with tiered packages (Basic, Pro and Ultimate), regional purchasing-power-parity pricing, team licenses and a bundle with The Joy of React. The 2021 early-access price was $129 (expected full price $349).
growth: Wrote interactive blog posts with live demos that spread on Twitter and developer forums; his most popular posts topped 100k visits
Converted Twitter followers into a newsletter before launch, including a free book (about 8k sign-ups) and an animated sign-up prompt on the blog
Built in public on Twitter from late 2020, sharing GIFs of the platform and content
Ran a one-week pre-sale at an early-access discount; the $50K target was hit in about 10 minutes
Built a custom learning platform with articles, videos, exercises, workshops and mini-games that set the course apart from video-only courses
Reused the platform and list for a second course, The Joy of React (2023)
moat: High production quality and interactive content on a custom platform, plus a trusted personal brand among front-end developers.
risks: Launch-driven revenue is lumpy. AI coding assistants may reduce how much developers feel they need to learn CSS fundamentals.

timeline.event: Starts building the course full time after leaving Gatsby
One-week early-access pre-sale (Mar 10-16); ~$550K against a $50K target
Continues building remaining modules for full release
Launches The Joy of React in early access (Jan 23)

lessons: A year of free, high-quality teaching content builds the trust that makes a pre-sale work
Pre-selling a half-finished course funds the rest and validates price
Owning the platform allows interactive formats competitors on generic course hosts can't match
Set a modest target; a realistic goal makes the decision to keep going clear

rebuild.idea: An interactive course teaching SQL and data modeling specifically to product managers and analysts in non-tech companies
rebuild.why: Many business staff now query data with AI help but lack fundamentals to check results; most SQL courses target developers or data scientists.
mvp: Publish 3 interactive blog posts with in-browser SQL playgrounds on common business questions
Collect emails with a free 'SQL mistakes that give wrong numbers' checklist
Pre-sell the first 3 modules at an early-access price for one week
Deliver module 1 within 2 weeks of the pre-sale
rebuild.fit: A data analyst or engineer who writes clearly and can build simple web interactives
rebuild.pricing: One-time purchase with a ~$99 early-access pre-sale, then $199-$349 tiers at full launch, plus team licenses.
rebuild.market: Buyers are product managers, ops and marketing analysts at non-tech companies, often on a training budget, reached through LinkedIn posts, SEO on interactive articles and a newsletter. Competitors include DataCamp, Mode's SQL tutorial, Codecademy, Udemy courses and free AI assistants.
